_about: The spec of kitcut.ai's first template (studio/templates.py make --spec): what it is, what the film keeps of its sample (keep, generic), when the sample is the person's own event (identity), and its author's notes to Claude. Its film is projects/websummit-speakers (local: the code is ours, the sample's logo and photos are Web Summit's and its speakers'). v5 (2026-09-30): no form -- a person says what they want, attaches what they have, and Claude finds the rest (on the web when it decides to); the template is the example it remakes.
title: Conference speaker promo
description: A 26-second promo for a conference or summit, told as a trip: your logo, a split-flap departures board with the city, dates and venue, a paper plane, your featured speakers on a turning carousel, a boarding pass and the poster. Music only, no narration.
author: KitCut
example: A promo for PGConf.EU 2026 (pgconf.eu). Feature the keynote speakers.
brief:
A 26-second speaker promo with no narration, told as a trip to the event, every beat on a hit of the music: the logo on its card over turning tiles, the dive into the accent colour, the split-flap departures board (city, dates, venue), the paper plane, the carousel that turns to each featured speaker while the name block turns with it, the boarding pass with its stamp, and the poster. People are black-and-white cut-outs on the brand's own colours.

The board has 10 cells a row: a city, dates or venue longer than that is shortened to fit (event.venue_short), never cut off. Names on the name block are fitted to it; a very long one may take a smaller size or two lines. A logo whose symbol can be drawn in code (content.logo.mark: its two shapes as polygons on one baseline and the point to dive into; content.logo.letters: the column spans of its letters) rises and dives as in the original; without them the whole logo wipes on and the film dives into a disc of the accent. Measure and add them only when the logo has a clear symbol and there is time; the fallback is fine.

The ring holds up to 24 people (fewer are repeated round it); the first five are the featured, each with a name, role and company. The tagline is up to three short lines, and the poster's last tagline word is in the accent colour. Keep the clock: the carousel always makes five stops, whatever the number of featured speakers.
